objectives: "The objective of the course is to introduce students the basic thermodynamic properties, the concepts of mass and energy conservation, the concepts of equilibrium, the laws of thermodynamics, and the thermodynamic differences between ideal and real systems. This course will also help students master those thermodynamics fundamentals and apply them, along with the equations of state and/or thermodynamics data in table or diagram forms, to solving the related engineering problems."
content:
"The topics to be discussed in this course include:

Introduction to Thermodynamics
Conservation of Mass
Conservation of Energy
Entropy: An Additional Balance Equation
The Thermodynamic Properties of Real Substance
Equilibrium and Stability in One-Component Systems
The Thermodynamics of Multicomponent Mixtures
Estimation of The Gibbs Energy and Fugacity of a Component in a Mixture
Vapor-Liquid Equilibrium in Mixtures"
books: "Chemical, Biochemical, and Engineering Thermodynamics, 5th Edition by Stanley Sandler, Wiley, ISBN 978-1-11992-349-7"
